dbsp.title: Palomar Hale 5.08 m / DBSP (Double Spectrograph at the Cassegrain focus: a dichroic behind the slit splits the light into two separate spectrographs, blue and red, each with a Cassegrain collimator, a reflection grating, a camera and a CCD)
dbsp.recommended_preset: Two entries of the instrument DBSP: blue 600/4000 and red 316/7500, both behind the D55 dichroic; see recommended_presets.

recommended_presets.name: Palomar / DBSP blue, 600/4000, D55, 1″
recommended_presets.basis: G = 600 l/mm blazed 4000 A and the blue camera 9 in = 228.6 mm, psi = 38.5 deg (POV, PYP; OG82: 38.333 deg); the dichroic D55; lamC = 4400 A is CHOSEN (the middle of the D55 blue band 3200-5500 A), not sourced; CCD 23 with 4096 along the dispersion (PDS).

recommended_presets.name: Palomar / DBSP red, 316/7500, D55, 1″

collimator_onaxis.value: ON-AXIS (Cassegrain: the arriving beam passes through a hole in the primary and the secondary stands in the middle of the collimated beam; no tilt)

alternatives.quote: before entering collimators through holes in the collimator primaries

alternatives.quote: The primaries of the Cas- segrain collimators produce second pupils between the gratings and the camera corrector plates

collimator_onaxis.note: DEPLOY GATE (evidence): INFERRED from the text plus the layout figures. A Cassegrain collimator is coaxial by construction: the secondary (hole in the primary 54 mm = the cage's shadow) sits on the axis of the collimated beam, so the beam returns along the incoming axis (colTilt 0). Fig. 1 (OG82, PDF p. 4) and the 'Raytrace of DBSP Red' (RTF) both draw the ring-shaped primary with the arriving beam in its hole and the secondary on its axis; nothing is tilted. The slit does NOT stand in the returning beam (the dichroic and the prism blocks fold the beam to the collimator's hole), which is the other on-axis geometry in the explorer (Hectospec, DESI). The 'field points +/-1 arcmin' in RTF are off-axis field points, not an off-axis collimator.

alternatives.quote: The light then passes through field lenses, into prisms, and through filters before entering collimators

collimator_field_lenses.note: The shapes (blue: 45-degree face turning the beam down; red: parallelogram shifting the beam sideways) are read from OG82 Fig. 1; the text calls them 'separating prisms' and 'quartz blocks'.

collimator_grating_distance.name: Secondary-to-grating distance
collimator_grating_distance.quote: The gratings are mounted approximately 49 cm below the Cassegrain collimator secondaries
collimator_grating_distance.note: 'approximately'. The RTF raytrace, scaled by the 146 mm beam, shows 600 mm (FIGURE READ-OFF, 24 percent longer; that figure is the later red-side drawing). The recommended layLen uses the SOURCED 490 mm.

collimator_primary_secondary.name: Collimator primary-to-secondary spacing
collimator_primary_secondary.derived: MEASURED: in Fig. 1 the primary's face is at y = 392 px and the secondary's quartz plate at y = 793 px (130 dpi page raster), 401 px; the scale is the 146 mm collimated beam (rims x = 148 and 300 px, 152 px; 0.96 mm/px): 401 x 0.96 = 385 mm. The RTF raytrace, scaled the same way (beam 67.5 px, primary x = 255, secondary plate x = 441.5, 186 px at 2.16 mm/px), gives 402 mm. Adopted 390 mm, +/- 15 mm.

collimator_hole_size.name: Hole in the primary / secondary size (the cage shadow)
collimator_hole_size.derived: MEASURED: the gap between the two halves of the blue primary is 86 px at 200 dpi (x = 207 to 293 px) and the beam rims are 233 px apart (x = 130 and 363): 146 mm x 86 / 233 = 54 mm; the central obstruction in the collimated beam is therefore 0.37 of the beam, the 0.36 of the 72-inch prime-focus cage on a 5080 mm aperture (hale.md; text: 'no larger than the shadow of the prime-focus cage'). Primary outside diameter 275 px = 172 mm.

collimator_two_arms.derived: MEASURED (axis separation): blue hole center x = 250 px, red hole center x = 568 px (200 dpi crop), 318 px x (146/233) = 199 mm.

grating_angle_definition.name: Definition of the grating angle
grating_angle_definition.value: the angle between the incident beam (from the collimator) and the grating normal, theta_i; the camera sits at theta_m = psi - theta_i on the other side; a (sin theta_m - sin theta_i) = m lambda in the page's sign convention (the explorer's alpha = t + psi/2 incident, beta = t - psi/2, same physics)
grating_angle_definition.quote: is called the grating angle, and is the angle between the incident optical beam (from the collimator) and the normal to the grating

alternatives.value: grating angle 0 = grating perpendicular to the incident beam; positive turns the face toward the camera
alternatives.quote: Grating angle = 0 puts the grating perpendicular to the incident beam from the collimator

alternatives.value: a grating angle of 29.5 deg appears in the red-channel throughput example
alternatives.quote: at a grating angle of 29.5°

grating_angle_definition.derived: DERIVED check of the sign: red 600 l/mm, psi = 35 deg, grating angle 29.5 deg: |sin(35 - 29.5) - sin 29.5| / 600 per mm = 6620 A, inside the D55 red band, so the incidence angle is the LARGER of the two angles, as in the explorer's alpha = t + psi/2 (alpha > |beta|).

blaze_reconciliation.name: Why POV's blazes differ from PDS's for four gratings
blaze_reconciliation.value: POV lists the blaze peak at the instrument's camera-collimator angle: lambda_peak = lambda_blaze x cos(psi/2)

blaze_reconciliation.derived: INFERRED, with DERIVED arithmetic: 600/4000 blue x cos(19.25 deg) = 3776 (POV 3780); 316/7500 red x cos(17.5 deg) = 7153 (POV 7150); 600/10000 red = 9537 (POV 9500); 1200/5000 blue = 4720 (POV 4700). All four POV values are the PDS nominal (Littrow) blaze shifted by cos(psi/2), exactly the explorer's blaze-peak rule (web/app.js: m lambda = 2 sin(delta) cos(psi/2) / G). It does NOT hold for 300/3990 (POV 3990; the rule gives 3767), 1200/7100, 1200/9400 or 158 (POV 7560 vs 7500; the rule gives 7153), so the reconciliation is partial; for those the two pages simply disagree or round.

conflicts: **Cassegrain focal ratio and scale**: f/15.7 and 2.5 arcsec/mm (OG82, mutually inconsistent: f/15.7 on 5080 mm is 2.586 arcsec/mm; 2.5 is f/16.24) vs 2.57 arcsec/mm at the slit (PDS, f/15.80) vs f/16 and 2.538 arcsec/mm (hale.md from the 3200-inch focal length) vs the collimator's 2311.4 / 146 = f/15.83 (2.565 arcsec/mm). The recommended entry takes F = 15.83 so that the collimator and both pixel scales are right (0.3890 and 0.2917 arcsec/px against 0.389 and 0.293).

**Blue camera-collimator angle**: 38 deg 20 arcmin = 38.333 deg (OG82 Sec. III.B) vs 38.50 deg (POV Sec. 4.c; PypeIt). The recommended entry uses 38.5 (current docs); the dispersion changes by 0.15 percent.

**Blaze wavelengths**: PDS (7500, 3990, 7500, 4000, 10000, 5000, 7100, 9400 for 158, 300, 316, 600b, 600r, 1200b, 1200, 1200) vs POV (7560, 3990, 7150, 3780, 9500, 4700, 7100, 9400). Four of the differences are the cos(psi/2) shift of the blaze peak (INFERRED, above); 158 (7500 vs 7560; K11 also 7560) is not. The explorer takes the Littrow blaze from PDS (7500 for the 158).

**Dispersions that differ by one unit**: 158/7500 red 202 (PDS) vs 201 (POV); 158 second order blue 134 vs 135; 1200 blue 36 vs 36 and 35 (9400); 600 blue 72 vs 71. The model gives 201.5, 71.3 and 35-36 (DERIVED).
**Slit**: 125 arcsec long, 0.5/1.0/2.0 wide plus seven apertures (OG82, 1982) vs 128 arcsec, eight widths 0.5-10 (PDS, POV). The preset uses the current slit.

**Red camera**: Schmidt f/1.0, 152 mm, scale reduction 15.2, 35 deg 00 arcmin, 178 mm corrector (OG82) vs a 12 in seven-element lens camera (since 1995; PDS, POV, K11). Reduction now 7.6. The 1982 instrument is recorded alongside; the preset uses the current camera.

**Wavelength ranges**: 1982 design: blue 3200-5200 A, red 5200-10,000 A, usable to 10,400 A (OG82) vs now blue < 3000-7000 A and red 4700-11000 A for the instrument (PDS); per exposure the chip and dichroic set the range (a D55 pair covers ~3200-5500 A blue and 5500-11,000 A red).
**Dichroic nominal vs measured**: D52 nominal 5200 (PDS) but 50 percent transmission at 5320 A (FIGURE READ-OFF); D55 5500 vs 5490. For the arms view the preset uses the D55 nominal 5500 A.

**Detector orientation**: PDS 'CCD 23: 2048 x 4096 (in the 4096 dispersion axis)' vs K11 Table 1 'E2V 4096 x 2048' for the same device (2005): the same chip described along its long or short axis. The explorer entry is Nx (dispersion) 4096, Ny 2048.
**Slit-to-grating drawing distance**: 490 mm (OG82 text, 'approximately') vs ~600 mm (RTF scaled by the 146 mm beam; FIGURE READ-OFF, the later red-side drawing).

**Unvignetted field**: 128 arcsec slit length (PDS) vs 'about 120 x 70 arcsec' unvignetted field for all cameras (POV Sec. 4.c) vs 125 x 62 arcsec (OG82 design). The numbers do not agree; the 120 arcsec is the current guider-field number.
notes: **Setting menu**: two arms of one instrument, in the existing convention (a Preset line `DBSP`, Setting entries `blue, 600/4000` and `red, 316/7500`), each with the D55 dichroic. Optional further Settings (all DERIVED from the grating tables and the same optics, not separately sourced): blue 300/3990, blue 1200/5000, red 158/7500, red 600/10000, red 1200/7100. Note that the explorer's 'All arms' view takes one preset per arm, so the extra gratings would be alternate arms of the same dichroic tree, as MIKE's 'red' and 'blue' are single entries.

**Why D55 and 600/4000 + 316/7500**: D55 is the dividing wavelength the designers planned (OG82 Sec. II.E); PypeIt has arc templates for the pairs 600/4000 (blue; D55, D68) with 316/7500 (red; D55) and 600/10000 (red; D55), and the one setup described in detail in the literature that was found (C22, HAT-P-1b, 2012) uses D52 with 600/4000 and 316/7500. This is an INFERRED popularity, not a census. For the 1982 as-built values: dichroic 5200 A (OCLI cold mirror), blue camera 38.333 deg, red camera a 152 mm Schmidt at 35 deg; in 1982 the red scale reduction was 15.2, so a 0.5 arcsec slit was 13 um on the detector.

**Explorer check (DERIVED; web/physics.js required read-only from a scratchpad script; no project file changed)**: blue (D = 5.08 m, F = 15.83, W = 146 mm, G = 600, blaze 4000 A, psi = 38.5 deg, f_cam = 228.6 mm, 15 um pixels, lamC 4400 A): fcol 2311.2 mm, plate 2.565 arcsec/mm, pixel scale 0.3890 arcsec, dispersion 1.0727 A/px (71.5 A/mm), incidence 27.29 deg, diffraction -11.21 deg, Rs 1761 for a 1 arcsec slit (slit image 2.33 px: the anamorphic factor 1.10 narrows it), range 3200-6606 A. **Grating geometry (important for the model)**: the explorer's alpha = t + psi/2 (incidence larger than the camera-side angle) matches DBSP: the Palomar 'grating angle' is the incidence angle and the sign check on the 29.5-degree red example gives a wavelength of 6620 A. At 4400 A the blue grating angle is 27.3 deg. The grating is read by dial 'to about 1 arc min' (OG82).

**Beam size in the model**: the preset W = 146 mm is the collimated beam; the grating's anamorphic factor makes the diffracted beam 158-161 mm wide (blue 4400 A: 161 mm, F_cam needed 1.42; red 7500 A: 158 mm, F_cam needed 1.93). The OG82 blue corrector (175 x 216 mm) was made larger 'to allow for the spectrograph dispersion'; the red Epps lens aperture is NOT FOUND.

**On the 'Cassegrain collimator' drawing**: the explorer draws a mirror collimator that folds the beam back past the slit (or, with colTilt 0, on the axis with the slit in the returning beam). DBSP's collimator is neither: the arriving beam passes through a hole in the primary, strikes the small secondary on the quartz plate, returns to the primary and leaves as a 146 mm beam with a 54 mm central obstruction, travelling the same direction as the arriving light (a folded, on-axis, two-mirror collimator, primary and secondary 390 mm apart). The state's colTilt = 0 and layLen are the closest representation; the drawing's one mirror cannot show the second mirror, the hole, or the quartz plate.

**Throughput caveat**: PDS's 12 percent is 'sky-to-detector' (telescope and atmosphere-free spectrograph and detector as measured on the sky), K11's 37 percent peak is spectrograph + detector with the telescope mirrors and atmosphere removed. They are different quantities and are not compared with the model.

**The dispersion tables are at the blaze wavelength**: POV Sec. 4.c says 'the values there are representative, evaluated at the blaze wavelength, but dispersion is a very slow function of wavelength.' The model reproduces them at lamC = blaze for the arms that blaze within the band.
**Privacy**: all web fetches used a generic User-Agent; the ADS key was used only in the Authorization header; no personal data was sent.
